gloss: to go along together; to be partners in life

definitions.gloss: to go along together; to accompany each other
definitions.explanation: For two or more people to travel through something together — literally along a road, or figuratively through life as a married couple. Now a dated, literary word; the derived noun {連|つ}れ{合|あ}い (spouse) is far more common.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{連|つ}れ{合|あ}った{夫婦|ふうふ}。
examples.english: A couple who have spent many years together.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}から{連|つ}れ{合|あ}ってきた。
examples.english: The two of them have been together since they were young.

examples.japanese: {苦|くる}しい{時代|じだい}を{連|つ}れ{合|あ}って{生|い}きてきた{二人|ふたり}の{絆|きずな}は{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: The bond between the two, who lived through hard times side by side, is strong.

notes:
{連|つ}れる (to take along) + {合|あ}う (to do mutually), so literally 'to take each other along.' The verb itself is old-fashioned and mostly appears in writing; learners meet it chiefly as the source of the everyday noun {連|つ}れ{合|あ}い.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長年|ながねん}{連|つ}れ{合|あ}う: to be together for many years
- {連|つ}れ{合|あ}って{歩|ある}く: to walk along together

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {連|つ}れ{添|そ}う: to be married to — the usual modern verb for living as a married couple
- {付|つ}き{合|あ}う: to associate with, to date — everyday word for keeping company
